title: Biologist
statementMd:
SmallR is a biologist. Her latest research finding is how to change the sex of dogs. In other words, she can change female dogs into male dogs and vice versa.

She is going to demonstrate this technique. Now SmallR has $*n*$ dogs, the costs of each dog's change may be different. The dogs are numbered from 1 to $*n*$. The cost of change for dog $*i*$ is $*v*_{*i*}$ RMB. By the way, this technique needs a kind of medicine which can be valid for only one day. So the experiment should be taken in one day and each dog can be changed at most once.

This experiment has aroused extensive attention from all sectors of society. There are $*m*$ rich folks which are suspicious of this experiment. They all want to bet with SmallR forcibly. If SmallR succeeds, the $*i*$-th rich folk will pay SmallR $*w*_{*i*}$ RMB. But it's strange that they have a special method to determine whether SmallR succeeds. For $*i*$-th rich folk, in advance, he will appoint certain $*k*_{*i*}$ dogs and certain one gender. He will think SmallR succeeds if and only if on some day the $*k*_{*i*}$ appointed dogs are all of the appointed gender. Otherwise, he will think SmallR fails.

If SmallR can't satisfy some folk that isn't her friend, she need not pay him, but if someone she can't satisfy is her good friend, she must pay $*g*$ RMB to him as apologies for her fail.

Then, SmallR hope to acquire money as much as possible by this experiment. Please figure out the maximum money SmallR can acquire. By the way, it is possible that she can't obtain any money, even will lose money. Then, please give out the minimum money she should lose.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$, $*g*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{4}, 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ *g* ≤ 10^{4})$. The second line contains $*n*$ integers, each is 0 or 1, the sex of each dog, 0 represent the female and 1 represent the male. The third line contains $*n*$ integers $*v*_{1}, *v*_{2}, ..., *v*_{*n*}$ $(0 ≤ *v*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4})$.

Each of the next $*m*$ lines describes a rich folk. On the $*i*$-th line the first number is the appointed sex of $*i*$-th folk (0 or 1), the next two integers are $*w*_{*i*}$ and $*k*_{*i*}$ $(0 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}, 1 ≤ *k*_{*i*} ≤ 10)$, next $*k*_{*i*}$ distinct integers are the indexes of appointed dogs (each index is between 1 and $*n*$). The last number of this line represents whether $*i*$-th folk is SmallR's good friend (0 — no or 1 — yes).

## Output

Print a single integer, the maximum money SmallR can gain. Note that the integer is negative if SmallR will lose money.
statementZhMd:
## 题目描述

SmallR 是一名生物学家。她最近的研究成果是改变狗的性别。换句话说，她可以将母狗变成公狗，反之亦然。

她准备展示这项技术。现在 SmallR 有 $*n*$ 只狗，改变每只狗所需的费用可能不同。这些狗的编号为 1 到 $*n*$。改变第 $*i*$ 只狗的性别需要花费 $*v*_{*i*}$ 元人民币。顺便一提，这项技术需要一种只能维持一天药效的药物。因此，实验必须在一天内完成，并且每只狗最多只能被改变一次。

这项实验引起了社会各界的广泛关注。有 $*m*$ 位富人对这项实验持怀疑态度。他们都强行要和 SmallR 打赌。如果 SmallR 成功，第 $*i*$ 位富人将支付给 SmallR $*w*_{*i*}$ 元人民币。不过奇怪的是，他们有一种特殊的方法来判断 SmallR 是否成功。对于第 $*i*$ 位富人，他会事先指定 $*k*_{*i*}$ 只狗以及一种性别。当且仅当在某一天这 $*k*_{*i*}$ 只指定的狗全都变成指定的性别时，他才会认为 SmallR 成功；否则，他会认为 SmallR 失败。

如果 SmallR 无法满足某位并非她朋友的富人的要求，她不需要赔钱；但如果无法满足的那个人是她的好朋友，她必须支付 $*g*$ 元人民币作为失败的道歉。

因此，SmallR 希望通过这次实验获得尽可能多的钱。请你求出 SmallR 能获得的最大金额。顺便一提，她可能一分钱也得不到，甚至还会亏钱。此时，请输出她最少需要亏损的金额。

## 输入

第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$、$*g*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{4}, 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ *g* ≤ 10^{4})$。第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数，每个整数为 0 或 1，表示每只狗的性别，其中 0 表示母狗，1 表示公狗。第三行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*v*_{1}, *v*_{2}, ..., *v*_{*n*}$ $(0 ≤ *v*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4})$，表示改变每只狗性别的费用。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行每行描述一位富人。第 $*i*$ 行的第一个数是第 $*i*$ 位富人指定的性别（0 或 1），接下来的两个整数是 $*w*_{*i*}$ 和 $*k*_{*i*}$ $(0 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}, 1 ≤ *k*_{*i*} ≤ 10)$，接下来是 $*k*_{*i*}$ 个互不相同的整数，表示指定狗的编号（每个编号均在 1 到 $*n*$ 之间）。本行的最后一个数表示第 $*i*$ 位富人是否是 SmallR 的好朋友（0 — 否，1 — 是）。

## 输出

输出一个整数，表示 SmallR 能获得的最大金额。注意，如果 SmallR 会亏钱，则该整数为负数。
